_comment: Per-individual-model prompting knowledge, read by prompt-kit.js. Every entry below is a Phase-1 SEED, not a research result: render/example text is inherited verbatim from prompt-kit.js's family-level AGENT_PROFILES (the only real data that exists yet), and tier/reasoning are best-informed classification, not verified findings. researched:false means exactly that — this model has not been individually researched. The Phase-3 pipeline (tools/model-research.js, not built yet) is what flips entries to researched:true with model-specific render text and a real source. Do not treat a seed entry's render text as if it were already model-specific — it is deliberately identical to its family's AGENT_PROFILES entry until real research replaces it.

models.render: Render every section as an XML-style tag named after the section, lowercase, hyphenated if multi-word (e.g. <task>, <context>, <done-when>). Claude follows this precisely and reasons well over clearly-scoped, nuanced instructions — a section can contain a short nested list where that adds clarity.

example.input: write something for my landlord about the broken heater
example.output:
<role>Tenant writing a maintenance request</role>
<context>The heater in the user's rental unit is broken. No other details were given about how long, severity, or prior contact.</context>
<task>Write a clear, polite message to the landlord reporting the broken heater and requesting repair.</task>
<constraints>Do not invent specifics not given — no assumed dates, no assumed prior complaints, no assumed lease terms.</constraints>
<output-format>A short message, ready to send as-is (email or text), professional but not stiff.</output-format>

models.notes: Seed inherited from the claude family profile. Anthropic's current general guidance (not Opus-5-specific) de-emphasizes mandatory XML and heavy role-framing for modern models — worth folding in once this entry is actually researched.

models.render: Minimal. State the goal, constraints, and desired output shape in plain sentences. No manual chain-of-thought instruction, no few-shot example, no nested structure — this model reasons internally and external scaffolding measurably hurts it. All instructions go in the user turn, never a system-role persona.
models.notes: The one entry actually backed by real primary-source research this session (not a family-inherited seed) — DeepSeek's own documented guidance is explicit that even Claude's mild XML tagging should be avoided here, which is the concrete proof that same tier+reasoning classification does not mean same render text.

verified.result: no clear difference on these fixtures (proposed: 12 issues/1w avg, baseline: 12 issues/1w avg)
